alphabet_rows_to_retain.reason: H mathfrak F is a different alphabet from the final cursive/script F. H's sty imports ordinary amsfonts/mathrsfs and does not alias mathfrak to mathscr or mathcal. The recorded decisions describe curved, looped manuscript arms and explicitly reject a Gothic body. Under the user's requirement to retain alphabets, this is not merely equivalent command syntax. The unresolved choice between mathscr and mathcal must remain uncertain.

The final adds explicit plain/calligraphic uncertainty to H's certain mathcal M or mathcal L. The difference is the surviving alternative and uncertainty state, not an assertion that the final has proved H's alphabet wrong. Retain in the doubt/change apparatus; consider classifying as other/uncertainty instead of a resolved symbol misreading.

alphabet_scope_reviews_not_definite_macr.recommendation: Check whether the broad figure-set alphabet row already explicitly covers the row-d subscript and set name. If it does, avoid double counting this occurrence; otherwise it remains a real alphabet difference.

This row explicitly states that the first-occurrence L|mathcal L uncertainty governs both repeated Fig operators and that no new alphabet decision was made. Prefer linking the repeated occurrences to 004-05 rather than treating them as fresh resolved H errors. This is a scope/deduplication issue, not proof that L and mathcal L are globally interchangeable.

H already reads the actual letter F before (M), so the evidence 'F rather than P' does not establish an H letter-reading error. Any H difference here is only the alphabet policy already covered by the recurring F/M rows. Retain the C-side F/P adjudication; merge or cross-reference the H alphabet component if those global rows include this occurrence.

macro_conversion_rules: H struck and final deleted, or H add and final inserted, are equivalent only when the same text has the same state and attachment. No row consisting solely of those aliases was found.
H uncertain is defined as editorial underline. It must not be confused with the manuscript's own underline; a changed certainty state remains a real apparatus difference.

H emph is used for Grothendieck's own emphasis according to the sty comments. Translating the same marked span to uline is a convention conversion, but differing span, absent emphasis, or insertion state remains substantive.
Guillemets versus paired high quotation strokes are not equivalent macro spellings of an unchanged mark; the user explicitly requires the literal quotation shapes.
No blanket normalization of mathfrak, mathscr, mathcal or ordinary Latin/Greek case is justified by H's supplied sty.
